Guide | section: Story Board, Outline and Beats | text: Story in the left navigation has the tabs Page, Board, Outline, Characters, Timeline and, for episodic projects, Episodes. Convert to Scene makes a new Scene Card from the Beat text, and the Beat stays behind marked Converted. The Outline shows the same Acts, Sequences and cards as a list. Build Screenplay turns Scene Cards into screenplay scenes, and a card needs a scene heading for that. After the build, the card and the screenplay scene are separate.

Guide | section: Drafts and locking | text: A screenplay has one or more drafts. Creating a new draft copies the current one so earlier drafts stay unchanged. You can compare two drafts to see scenes added, removed, changed or moved. A draft can be locked as the shooting draft; a locked draft cannot be edited directly, so start a revision to make changes. The assistant cannot bypass a lock either.
Guide | section: Shooting schedule and shooting days | text: The shooting schedule places scenes of the Production Source onto shooting days. You create shooting days in Production, then move scene strips onto them. Unscheduled scenes are eligible scenes that are not on any shooting day yet. The assistant can explain conflicts or suggest groupings, but it never reorders scenes or changes dates on its own.
</facts>

Label the kind of answer the person wants from a film-production assistant. Reply with one label only, from: lookup, list, count, explain, relation, compare, brainstorm, navigate, change, help, chat.
lookup: one fact (who plays X, the phone of Y, where scene 4 is set).
list: several items listed.
count: a number of things.
explain: explain or summarise a scene, an act or the story.
relation: how people or things are connected.
compare: planned against actual, one thing against another, a difference.
brainstorm: ideas, improvements, options.
navigate: open or go to a screen, scene or file.
change: add, edit, delete or create something in the project.
help: how to use the app.
chat: greetings, thanks, anger, complaints with no question.
If the message corrects an earlier answer, label what it asks for.
If the message only names something, label it like the previous message.
Examples:
"who is the stunt coordinator" -> lookup
"planned against actual for transport" -> compare
"describe the opening scene" -> explain
"how are Rhea and her brother related" -> relation
"two ideas for a better ending" -> brainstorm
"add a task to book the van" -> change
"where do I turn on dark mode" -> help
"this is useless" -> chat
